offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst

## 1. Our offer to you

Dear {{employee.full_name}}, we are pleased to offer you the job of Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst at Absa Group. This is a permanent position. Your start date is 1 December 2026. Your place of work is Sandton, head office.

## 2. What you will do

You will support Coverage Bankers in managing a portfolio of corporate and institutional clients. You will prepare client briefs, pitch materials and account plans, and track client activity, opportunities and pipeline. You will do financial statement analysis, build financial models and forecasts, and perform credit analysis and risk assessments. You will also support lending, advisory and capital markets deals, coordinate with Risk, Legal and Product teams, prepare documents for deal approvals and credit committees, and keep to KYC / AML and internal risk and compliance rules. In addition, you will do industry and competitor research, watch macroeconomic trends, and produce insight reports and sector updates.

## 3. Pay and hours

Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month. We pay by EFT on the 25th of the month. PAYE and UIF of 1% will be deducted. You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00, with a meal break of 60 minutes.

## 4. Leave and probation

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave in each 12-month leave cycle. You get 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle and 3 days' family responsibility leave a year. Maternity leave is at least 4 consecutive months and parental leave is 10 consecutive days. The first 3 months are a probationary period.

## 5. How to accept

This offer is open until 30 November 2026. Please send us your ID and your qualifications. If you have questions, email hr@example.co.za.

## 6. Acceptance

I, {{employee.full_name}}, accept this offer on {{date_signed}}.

contract.markdown:
# Contract of employment — Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Sandton (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst. The Employee's duties include: Support Coverage Bankers in managing a portfolio of corporate / institutional clients; Prepare client briefs, pitch materials, and account plans; Track client activity, opportunities, and pipeline; Maintain strong understanding of client strategies, industries, and financial performance; Conduct financial statement analysis (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow); Build and maintain financial models and forecasts; Perform credit analysis and risk assessments; Develop client profitability and return analysis; Assist with execution of lending, advisory, and capital markets transactions; Coordinate internal stakeholders (e.g., Risk, Legal, Product teams); Prepare documentation for deal approvals and credit committees; Support due diligence and data gathering processes; Ensure adherence to KYC / AML requirements; Ensure adherence to internal risk and compliance policies; Assist with regulatory submissions and audit requests where required; Work closely with product partners (e.g.: Corporate Finance, Transaction Banking, Markets, Treasury); Help structure integrated solutions aligned to client needs; Support cross-sell initiatives across the CIB platform; Conduct industry research and competitor analysis; Monitor macroeconomic trends affecting clients; Produce insight reports and sector updates. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Sandton, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

Signed at ____________ on {{date_signed}}.

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This clause names the two sides of the contract. The employer is Absa Group at 1 Main Road, Sandton. You are named with your identity number and your address.

You are appointed as Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst, and the clause lists the duties you must do. These include client support, financial and credit analysis, deal and documentation support, KYC / AML and compliance, work with product partners, and research and insight reports. The employer may also reasonably ask you to do other duties that fit this position.
Your employment starts on 1 December 2026. The job is permanent, so there is no set end date.

Your first 3 months are a probation period. During this time the employer checks your performance against what the job needs and must give you reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. At the end of probation your job may be confirmed, probation extended, or your employment ended, and a fair procedure must be followed.
You will work at Sandton, head office. That is your place of work under this contract.

You work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You take a 60-minute meal break after no more than five hours of continuous work. You also get at least 12 hours of rest in a row each day and at least 36 hours of rest in a row each week.

You are paid a basic salary of R18,000.00 a month, which works out to R103.85 for each ordinary hour. Payment is made monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments and no payments in kind are made.

You only work overtime if you agree, and it cannot be more than ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times your ordinary hourly wage, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. Sunday work is paid at double your ordinary wage (or one and a half times if you normally work Sundays), and public holiday work is paid at double.
PAYE and UIF of 1% will be taken off your pay. No other deduction may be made unless you agree in writing for a specific debt, or the law, a court order or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave in each 12-month cycle, taken at a time agreed with the employer and no later than six months after the cycle ends. You get 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle, but in your first six months you get one day for every 26 days worked; a medical certificate may be asked for if you are off more than two days in a row or more than twice in eight weeks. Maternity leave is at least 4 consecutive months, parental leave is 10 consecutive days, adoption and commissioning parental leave are as set out in the Act, and you get 3 days' paid family responsibility leave a year once you have worked longer than four months and work at least four days a week.

Either you or the employer can end the contract with written notice: one week if you have worked six months or less, two weeks if more than six months up to one year, and four weeks if more than one year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. The employer may still dismiss you immediately for a fair reason with a fair procedure, and both sides may agree to skip notice.
No bargaining council agreement applies to this business. No sectoral determination applies either.

You may not share or use confidential information of the employer, its clients or its suppliers. This applies while you work there and after you leave. The only exceptions are when you need it to do your job or when the law requires it.
No other documents form part of this contract. Only what is written in this contract counts.

This contract is the whole agreement on this subject, and any change must be written down and signed by both of you. If any term gives you less than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the better provision applies. The employer keeps these particulars for three years after your employment ends and will explain them to you if you ask.
This is the signature block. The employer's signatory signs for Absa Group, and you sign as the employee. The place of signing and the date signed are filled in.
